blocks.h2: Leaks and Old Pipe in Skokie Homes
blocks.intro: Many postwar Skokie homes were built with galvanized steel water pipe.

items.body: It slowly narrows, cuts pressure and eventually leaks at the threads.
Decades of repairs leave copper, galvanized and plastic joined together, and those transitions can leak.
A single leak can be repaired. When the whole system is failing, repiping is the long-term fix. If a pipe has burst, see [burst pipe repair](/skokie/burst-pipe-repair).
Old washer hoses and valves are common leak points.

blocks.h2: Leak and Pipe Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Do I need to repipe my whole house?
items.answer: Not always. If one section is leaking and the rest is sound, a repair is enough. If galvanized pipe is failing throughout, repiping makes sense.

items.q: How do I know if I have galvanized pipe?
items.preview: Gray metal pipe with threaded joints.
items.answer: Look at the pipes in the basement near the water heater. Gray steel pipe with threaded fittings is usually galvanized.

items.q: Can you find a leak without opening walls?
items.preview: We locate it first so openings stay small.
items.answer: We use listening equipment and pressure tests to narrow it down before opening anything.

items.preview: Sudden damage often, slow leaks often not.
items.answer: Policies vary. Check with your agent.

items.q: Can a leak raise my water bill a lot?
items.answer: Yes. A running toilet alone can waste a lot of water.

items.q: Can you replace galvanized pipe in stages?
items.answer: Yes. We can replace the worst sections first and plan the rest.

items.q: How much does pipe repair cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on the leak or the scope. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the leak or how much pipe needs replacing. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
